headline: Precious Metals and Energy Slump Across the Board on Hawkish Fed Signals
paragraphs: Commodities faced broad selling pressure today as hawkish Federal Reserve signals and pricing for expected interest rate hikes weighed heavily on the market. Gold fell 0.45 percent, extending its weekly decline to 4.00 percent and hitting a one-year low, while silver dropped 3.56 percent on the day and 7.47 percent for the week. Platinum retreated 1.36 percent and palladium lost 2.78 percent, pressured by a strengthening dollar and weak precious-metals sentiment.

Crude oil also recorded sharp losses, with Brent sliding 4.31 percent and WTI falling 3.96 percent. Natural gas dropped 4.37 percent, driven lower by milder weather and record US liquefied natural gas flows. Meanwhile, copper plunged 1.75 percent on the day and 3.96 percent for the week, hitting a four-month low as doubts grew about artificial intelligence data center demand alongside weak data out of China.
The euro traded at 1.1008 against the US dollar, reflecting a relatively stable currency exchange rate that kept euro-denominated commodity prices tracking their US dollar settlements closely.
